equity.level_reason: Only age and sex are used: age bounds define the population and age groups and sex are strata. The female-male contrast among ages 11–14 is interpreted as pandemic coping, not framed as social position.

level_alternative.reason: Sex-specific visit ratios with CIs are reported and interpreted for 11–14-year-olds, which could be read as group-specific SPD results.

ev.q: Cannabis-Involved Emergency Department Visits Among Persons Aged <25 Years Before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic
Large increases in cannabis-involved ED visit rates occurred among children aged ≤10 years, and among persons aged 11–14 years
rates among females aged 11–14 years increased more than they did among males.
This might indicate that females were more likely than males to use cannabis to cope with pandemic-related stress.

equity.equity_measurement: Age (≤10, 11–14, 15–24 years) and sex only; female-to-male visit ratios use males as referent. No race/ethnicity, SES or rurality data.

notes: Design inferred (none named): syndromic surveillance repeated by period. Visit ratios are hand-computed rate ratios (arithmetic); facility restriction by coefficient of variation is an exclusion rule, not a procedure. Rates are per 10,000 ED visits (a proportion of visits), so recorded as binary/categorical; mean weekly counts by period as count/rate.
view_issues: Text says '<10 years' and calls ≤10 visit ratios 'ratios per 10,000 ED visits'. Text says rates returned to baseline in the 'first half of the school year' yet cites weeks 12–23. Table 2's 1–11, 2020 ratio row repeats rates instead of dashes.
